source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, MSL ChemCam LIBS archive, master observation list msl_ccam_obs.csv
licence: NASA Planetary Data System, public domain. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/LANL/CNES/IRAP (ChemCam team)
notes: Names of the rocks, soils and other features ChemCam fired its laser at from each rover stop, with the list's free-text 'Target Type'. Only rows whose 'Type of Product' is '1-D Single laser' are counted; passive, dark, imaging-only and calibration-target rows are left out. Names and types are spelled as in the list. The list holds no chemistry: this layer says what was examined, not what it is made of. At most 12 names are stored per stop, the first ones observed; 'n' is the full count of distinct names there.
join_note: Joined by the list's own 'RMC Site' and 'RMC Drive' columns, which are the rover position counters that make up the stop id in data/site.json, so the join is exact and does not rely on the sol. The list's own distance column puts these laser targets 1.8 to 9.2 m from the mast (median 2.7 m), so each is placed at its stop.
coverage_note: Sols 19 to 4843. 77 laser rows (14 stop/target pairs) were taken at a site/drive that is not a stop in site.json and are left out.

fields.n: distinct laser targets at the stop
